FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Only PSG have collected more points than Nice across the last six Ligue 1 rounds, so the meeting of two in-form sides has the potential to be the game of the round. 

Match News and Current Form

Nice can profess to be one of Ligue 1’s most in-form sides at present after their 2-0 win against Angers prior to the international break secured a fifth victory in six top-flight matches (L1). That marks a remarkable turnaround in form for a side who’d only won five of their previous 34 Ligue 1 games (D13, L16) and affords them a shot at winning four matches in a row in this competition for the first time since March 2025. Three home league wins in succession should give them some confidence here, but they’ll have to overcome the psychological hurdle of failing to win any of their last seven Saturday-held league matches (D4, L3) if they’re to stretch that run to four for the first time since December 2023.

PSG may have made a slow start to the Ligue 1 campaign but it didn’t take them long to hit their stride and they now sit pretty in their customary position at the top of the table. Seven league wins in succession explain why, with those part of a wider run of 11 in a row in all competitions, the longest run across the top-five European leagues pre-round as the Parisians’ quest for a sixth Ligue 1 crown in succession gathers momentum. An impressive 14 wins from their last 16 Saturday-held away league games (L2) will certainly fuel belief they can keep that momentum going here, especially given one of them was a 4-0 triumph in last season's corresponding fixture. 

Head-to-Head History

PSG’s win in this fixture last term is one of seven they’ve managed in their last nine visits to Nice (D1, L1), while their pair of wins to nil in last season’s H2Hs allows them the chance to keep three successive Ligue 1 clean sheets against Nice for the first time ever.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Only PSG (66) have committed fewer fouls than Nice (95) in Ligue 1 this season.

Nice have collected a pre-round league-high 24 yellow cards this term.

PSG have scored in their last 23 competitive away games. 

PSG have netted 12 of their 15 Ligue 1 away goals this season in the second half. 

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Nice's Jonathan Clauss is set to make his 200th Ligue 1 appearance here - three of his last four goals for the club arrived after the hour mark, while he’s attempted the second most league shots of any Nice player this term. Ferran Torres has racked up more shots on target (15) than any other PSG player in Ligue 1 this season and has netted six of his seven goals for the club after the half-hour mark. 

Mohamed Abdelmonem is expected to miss out here for Nice. PSG’s Désiré Doué picked up an injury for France on international duty, but Nuno Mendes, Marquinhos and Ousmane Dembélé are all closing in on returns.

Betting Analysis

Backing a draw could be a good approach to take here as the formbook suggests there’s little to separate this pair.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Two teams who were in form before the international break look to enhance their European qualification prospects as Eintracht Frankfurt host Hoffenheim.

Match News and Current Form

A late equaliser secured Frankfurt a 2-2 draw at Paderborn and extended their unbeaten run to three games (W2, D1) before the international break. That fixture did highlight the struggles the Eagles are having at the back though, with the 20 league goals they have conceded at this stage a joint-high for the club over the last 50 years. Only seven of those strikes have come at home, and a return to Waldstadion should be a boost to manager Adi Hütter given he has tasted defeat there just once in 23 games as Frankfurt boss (W14, D8), winning each of the last two. 

Hoffenheim’s miserable start to the campaign left them in 17th place after five matches, but they have surged up the Bundesliga table thanks to a run of three wins in four matches (L1). The most recent of those was a 2-1 success against Schalke, which actually ended a run of three without a victory (D1, L2) in all competitions as Hoffenheim continue to juggle European commitments. Manager Christian Ilzer therefore knows his side, who have four points fewer than at the same stage of last season, still have plenty of work to do, particularly having lost on five of their last seven away outings (W1, D1). 

Head-to-Head History

Hoffenheim had won just two of the last 17 H2Hs (D4, L11) before winning last season’s corresponding fixture 3-1. Seventeen of those 18 meetings saw both teams score.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Nine of Frankfurt’s 11 fixtures this term produced over 2.5 goals.

Frankfurt have dropped the Bundesliga’s joint-second most points from winning positions ahead of this round (nine).

A pre-round joint-league high eight Hoffenheim matches have featured over 8.5 corners.

Only one team enter this round having conceded more first-half goals than Hoffenheim’s 14.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Noah Atubolu has made 3+ saves in nine of his last ten games for Frankfurt, but a 3-0 defeat while playing for Freiburg last term means he has never kept a clean sheet in five personal H2Hs against Hoffenheim. Only one player enters this round having committed more Bundesliga fouls than Hoffenheim’s Ozan Kabak (19), including at least two in his last three league appearances.

Frankfurt will be missing the suspended Elias Baum, while Hoffenheim could be without Bambasé Conté and Robin Hranáč.

Betting Analysis

The history books suggest to expect plenty of action at both ends when these two play, so both teams to score and over 2.5 goals might be worth a look.

Napoli and Torino face off with a maximum of one point separating them ahead of a Serie A matchday for only the second time since the start of the 1994/95 season, as both teams look to bounce back from identical three-game winless runs across all competitions (D1, L2).

Match News and Current Form

Napoli held Lazio to a 1-1 draw before the international break, but are now nine points adrift of Serie A’s top four ahead of this round of fixtures. The Partenopei have therefore created an unwanted piece of history with just five wins from their first 15 competitive games this season (D3, L7) - the first time that they have won so few matches at this stage of a campaign during the era of owner Aurelio De Laurentiis. Two of those three draws have come in their last two games at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, so Massimiliano Allegri’s men will be targeting a reaction, as Napoli haven't drawn three consecutive top-flight home matches since February 2010.

Torino also drew 1-1 (against Lecce) immediately before the international break, extending a three-game winless run that has erased the positives of three successive victories to begin October. The Maroons are nothing if not consistent though, having earned exactly 14 points after 11 matches for the fifth time in their last six Serie A campaigns. Ignazio Abate brings a resilient side to Naples, as Torino have lost on just one of their last four away trips (W2, D1), although both those wins have come against teams starting this weekend outside the top 15.

Head-to-Head History

Napoli have lost just two of the last 22 H2Hs (W15, D5) and have a similarly impressive home record against Torino, going unbeaten in their last 14 such games (W9, D5).

Torino conceded 2+ goals in 12 of their last 17 away matches.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Napoli’s Rasmus Højlund scored three times for Denmark during the international break, while six of his last eight goals for club or country have come after half-time. Ché Adams recorded an assist for Scotland during the break and set up Torino’s only goal in a 2-1 loss in last season’s corresponding fixture.

Napoli have a lengthy injury list, not helped by Giovanni Di Lorenzo missing their two games prior to the break. Torino pair Nikola Vlašić and Rafik Belghali may be absent here through injury.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Parma need to arrest their slide down the Serie A table, but they face a daunting test against an in-form Roma side with their sights set on the title.

Match News and Current Form

An early red card inside ten minutes against Bologna set Parma on their way to a fourth defeat in six matches (W1, D1), leaving Alberto Gilardino’s side just a point above the relegation zone over the international break. Parma can take some comfort in also having eight points after 11 rounds last term before eventually surviving, and they’ll hope the similarities don’t stop there as matchday 12 yielded a victory last term! That did come on the road though, and their fortunes haven’t been quite as good at home of late, as one win from their last seven such outings evidences (D2, L4).

A three-match winning streak in Serie A in which they scored 12 goals has helped Roma close the gap at the top of the table, leaving them just two points behind city rivals Lazio pre-round. Fans can therefore continue dreaming of a first league title in 25 years, a belief further fuelled by the fact that Roma have never before scored as many as the 31 goals they rattled in across their opening 11 Serie A matches this term. The Giallorossi have also scored at least twice in their last three competitive away matches, but having also conceded 2+ goals in each of those (W1, D1, L1), goals aren’t necessarily conducive to success for Roma.

Head-to-Head History

Roma have won four consecutive H2Hs and six of their last eight visits to Parma (L2), although their last two away H2H wins did come by a single-goal margin.

Parma are the only Serie A side yet to score inside the opening 30 minutes.

Only Venezia have failed to score more often than Parma (five) in Serie A this season.

Roma have led a joint-league-high seven games at half-time this season (HT: D3, L1).

Ahead of the round, only Inter have scored more than Roma’s 16 second-half goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

After netting his first goal for Parma against Bologna, Vincent Sierro has now scored each of his last six club goals after the break. Rodrigo Mora has scored each of his last nine club goals in victories, with Roma netting at least three times in his four goalscoring appearances in Serie A.

Parma are without the suspended Abdoulaye Ndiaye as well as newly-sidelined duo David Romero and Diego Carlos. Roma are missing Lorenzo Pellegrini.

Parma’s distinct lack of goals coupled with Roma’s free-scoring nature makes a punt on Roma to win both halves seem appealing.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Newcastle United go in search of a much-needed Premier League victory against table-toppers Arsenal, who will be looking to extend their excellent start to this season’s title defence.

Match News and Current Form

Newcastle United went into the latest international break struggling for winning consistency and on a run of just two victories across their last eight Premier League fixtures (D2, L4) following a 1-1 draw against Fulham. That form saw them enter this matchday a fraction off the European qualification pace in 12th spot, and a return to St James’ Park may not be welcome news as no side has lost more home top-flight matches than the Magpies in 2026 (seven). Their poor run even includes two successive 1-0 defeats on home soil, as many goalless displays as they had recorded across their prior 35 league home fixtures combined.

With nine wins from their opening ten league outings this season (L1), Arsenal have made a near-perfect start to their Premier League title defence. Another win would see them become just the fifth team to reach ten victories in as few as 11 games to start a campaign, and with each of those prior four teams going on to lift the title in the same season, the omens would be looking very good for the Gunners if they achieve that feat. Manager Mikel Arteta could also record a bit of personal history here too in the away dugout, as he has the opportunity to record a 159th Premier League victory and enter the top ten for most in the history of the competition. 

Head-to-Head History

Arsenal have won more Premier League games against only two sides than they have against Newcastle (38), though have lost three of their last five away league H2Hs.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

After going into the international break with a loss, Como will look to get back to winning ways when they host a Cagliari side who are looking to win multiple Serie A games on the bounce for just the second time this season.

Match News and Current Form

Como lost 2-0 to Inter Milan before the break, with that result ending a six-game winning run in all competitions. The Lariani are expected to bounce back here, as they haven’t lost consecutive Serie A matches since the last week of April, and defence could once again be their driving force, as Cesc Fàbregas’ men remain one of the most frugal sides this league campaign, having conceded only ten goals. Playing at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia may also help fashion Como’s resurgence, as they are unbeaten here in competitive action this season (W5, D1), including winning the last three in a row.

Fabio Pisacane’s Cagliari side have made a strong start to the season, with their five league wins (D1, L5) marking their best return at this stage since the 2019/20 campaign despite only ending a five-game winless run (D1, L4) - including four consecutive defeats - just before the break with a 1-0 win over Frosinone. Now looking to win back-to-back league games for the first time since a run of three consecutive Serie A victories in September, Cagliari’s away-day struggles could prove problematic in that quest, as they could lose four consecutive top-flight trips for the first time since December 2023, having already suffered three such defeats in a row.

Head-to-Head History

Como won the last H2H 2-1 in March 2026, but this corresponding fixture last season ended goalless, which is part of five draws across the last eight H2Hs (COM: W2, L1).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Como are the only side to have seen goals scored in the first ten minutes of their Serie A matches this season.

Como have conceded multiple goals only twice in their last 13 home Serie A games.

A joint-league low four matches involving Cagliari this season saw both teams score.

Eight of Cagliari’s last 11 away Serie A matches produced over 2.5 goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Lucas Da Cunha scored Como’s only goal in their last home fixture (W 1-0 vs Venezia) and also netted their winner in the 2-1 victory when these sides last met. Daniel Maldini could be the one leading the visitors’ reply, as his five Serie A goals this season have served as Cagliari’s last strike of the game, with three being the match winner.

Moise Kean’s return to action for Como was further postponed after another setback, while Yael Trepy was injured in Cagliari’s last match before the break.

The international break came at a good time for Rayo Vallecano, who have lost two of their last three La Liga games (W1), just one fewer than in their previous 15 such outings (W6, D6). Just two of those were at home where, despite playing at two different venues, Rayo have been beaten only once in 14 La Liga matches (W8, D5), with six of those wins accompanied by a clean sheet.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Coventry and Crystal Palace have both started their Premier League campaigns poorly, giving this the feel of a ‘relegation six-pointer’, which the visitors approach under new management.

Match News and Current Form

Coventry ended the last matchday just one place above the relegation zone, having lost at least seven of their opening ten league games of a campaign for only the third time in their history. Winning three of their last six league fixtures (L3) offers some hope but it also highlights their unpredictable nature, something that’s been particularly clear at home, where Frank Lampard’s men have won two league games by 2+ goals and lost the other three without scoring. A good start appears key for the Sky Blues then, as they’re one of two sides yet to recover a point from a losing position in the Premier League this season.

Bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace took action during the international break after a dreadful start to the campaign, appointing former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank to replace Pierre Sage. The Dane inherits a side who have suffered four consecutive league defeats and conceded 24 goals already, their highest tally at this stage since 1980/81. He may also have his work cut out to make an instant impact given that the Eagles have won just one away league fixture this term (D1, L3), drawing blanks in four of those games, while only two of Palace’s last 13 permanent managers won the first Premier League game they managed.

Head-to-Head History

This will be the first H2H since March 2012, with Coventry losing just one of the last four meetings (W2, D1), and unbeaten across the last four meetings they hosted (W2, D2).

Jack Rudoni has scored in three of Coventry’s last five league fixtures, leading his side for Premier League shots taken and chances created this term (both 17). Coventry appear to have no new injury concerns while Palace are without Jean-Philippe Mateta through suspension and Jørgen Strand Larsen is doubtful after suffering an injury while on duty with Norway.

Schalke are still looking for their first home goal of this Bundesliga campaign and look unlikely to get much respite from Stuttgart, who are eyeing up the European spots after their second clean sheet win of the Bundesliga season.

Match News and Current Form

Schalke’s 2-1 defeat to Hoffenheim before the international break extended their winless run to seven competitive matches (D2, L5) and kept them in the relegation zone with just six points, the same tally that the Royal Blues had after nine matches of their relegation-bound campaign in 2022/23. Head coach Miron Muslić is under pressure to move his side away from the danger zone and bring some long-awaited joy to the home supporters, who haven't seen their side score in four consecutive Bundesliga home outings. Extending that drought here would see Schalke make unwanted history by equalling St. Pauli’s all-time Bundesliga record of failing to score in the first five home games of a season.

Stuttgart earned their third consecutive win in domestic competitions when they defeated Werder Bremen 1-0 in their last match before the break. That included back-to-back wins in the Bundesliga, which earned the Reds as many wins and points as they had managed in the first seven matches of this season. Sebastian Hoeneß’ side have proven to be no pushovers on the road, winning four of their last six away matches in all competitions and establishing a 1-0 lead within half an hour in three of them, setting them up to draw first blood against their typically slow-starting opponents.

Head-to-Head History

This will be the 101st Bundesliga H2H and the first in more than three years. Schalke won the last meeting between these sides, forming the latest part of an impressive run of seven wins from the last 12 Bundesliga H2Hs (D4, L1).

He is also likely to score late, as eight of his last 11 Bundesliga goals have also come beyond the 60th minute.

Several players for both teams could miss out here, including Schalke’s Timo Becker and Stuttgart pair Angelo Stiller and Josha Vagnoman.

La Liga’s 111th Seville derby will be a top-half affair as Sevilla look to correct a slight wobble and narrow the eight-point gap to high-flying rivals Real Betis.

Match News and Current Form

Sevilla have lost touch with La Liga’s top four after collecting just five points from their last six games (W1, D2, L3), a downturn which followed an impressive 13 from the six prior. Squandering the lead in three of those games certainly didn’t help their cause, but they can still revel in their best start to a La Liga season since 2021/22. It’s unsurprising then that coach Luis García Plaza is hopeful of qualifying for Europe, though he’ll need to get significant improvement out of his side to take the next step here, as Sevilla have lost all three league games this term against sides starting the round above them.

Since the start of September, only league leaders Barcelona have beaten Real Betis (W6, D2), a run which has helped them record their highest total of wins (eight) after 12 La Liga games since winning the title in 1934/35 (ten). Manuel Pellegrini therefore has every reason to be confident in continuing his personal six-game unbeaten run in La Liga against García (W2, D4), particularly as his team are also unbeaten across their last four La Liga road trips (W2, D2) and could now record three consecutive away clean sheets for the first time since October 2022.

Head-to-Head History

Betis could post a second straight away H2H win for the first time since 2011/12 after losing eight of the 11 prior (W1, D2). It has been a tightly-contested match-up with only one of the last ten competitive derbies being decided by a 2+ goal margin.

Isaac Romero is Sevilla’s leading scorer this season and will be out to score in a second consecutive Seville derby - his last three home goals for the club arrived in the first half. Sevilla pair Marcão and Peque Fernández face a race against time to be fit here, as do Betis’ Cucho Hernández and Diego Llorente.

Elversberg may have lost 2-1 to Borussia Dortmund just before the international break, but their tally of 13 Bundesliga points (W4, D1, L4) is still a great return for a team that many tipped to go straight back down. Indeed, since the 1970s, only one side has scored more goals at this stage in their first-ever season in the division (Hoffenheim in 2008/09 with 24), while only Bayern Munich and Leipzig have found the net more often on average in German top-flight home matches this term. Freiburg are somewhat unlikely early-season title challengers after accumulating their joint-highest points tally at this stage of a Bundesliga campaign (19), with the latest three coming against Union Berlin (2-0) on matchday nine. The Breisgau Brazilians have also scored more goals in the division (20) after nine games in a season than ever before, while they have found the net in their last 12 top-flight encounters - the longest ongoing run of any Bundesliga side. After collecting the majority of their points this season at home (12 vs 7), they’ll now be desperate to stay in the title race by registering back-to-back league wins on the road for the first time since mid-April.
